items.question: What supreme identities define the primordial and ultimate personhood of Rāma?
premises: Rāma is the primeval person
Rāma is the great person
Rāma is the supreme person
items.inference: Rāma embodies primordial, great, and supreme personhood simultaneously.
items.plain_english: He is the primeval person, the great person, and likewise the supreme person.

items.question: What qualities of speech and demeanor characterize Rāghava's divine presence?
premises: Rāghava has a smiling face
Rāghava speaks in measured words
Rāghava speaks with fullness
items.inference: Rāghava's demeanor and speech express gentle, measured, and complete expression.
items.plain_english: Rāghava has a smiling face, speaks measuredly, and also speaks fully.

items.question: How does Rāma's apparent human conduct coexist with divine worship?
premises: Rāma's conduct appears human through illusion
Rāma is worshipped by the great god
items.inference: Despite appearing to act as a human by illusion, Rāma is worshipped by the great god.
items.plain_english: His conduct is that of a human by illusion, yet he is worshipped by the great god.

items.question: What physical and heroic attributes distinguish Rāma's embodied form?
premises: Rāma has dark limbs and is beautiful
Rāma is heroic
Rāma wears yellow garments and bears a bow
items.inference: Rāma's form combines beauty, heroism, and iconic martial attributes.
items.plain_english: He is dark-limbed, beautiful, heroic, clad in yellow garments, and bearing a bow.

items.question: What sacred act and moral purity are attributed to Rāma here?
premises: Rāma established a Śiva liṅga
Rāma is devoid of all multitudes of sin
items.inference: Rāma is both a founder of Śiva worship and completely free from sin.
items.plain_english: He is the establisher of the Śiva liṅga and is devoid of all multitudes of sin.

items.question: What transcendent metaphysical status is ascribed to Rāma's ultimate nature?
premises: Rāma is the supreme light
Rāma is the supreme abode
Rāma is the highest limit and beyond the supreme
items.inference: Rāma's nature transcends all limits as supreme light, abode, and beyond the supreme.
items.plain_english: He is the supreme light, the supreme abode, the highest limit, and beyond the supreme.

items.question: What is the extent and identity of the name collection just recited?
premises: The preceding verses constitute a set of names
The names belong to Rāmabhadra
The set numbers one hundred and eight
items.inference: The recited list is the one hundred and eight names of Rāmabhadra.
items.plain_english: Thus this is the hundred and eight names of Rāmabhadra.

items.question: What extent of accumulated sin is removed by reciting these names?
premises: The reciter is freed from all sins
These sins arose over hundreds of crores of aeons
items.inference: Reciting these names frees one from all sins accumulated over vast cosmic time.
items.plain_english: He is freed from all sins arising over hundreds of crores of aeons.

items.question: What transformative effects on hostile powers result from this recitation?
premises: Kings go to servitude
Fires go to gentleness
items.inference: The recitation subdues hostile rulers and pacifies destructive forces like fire.
items.plain_english: Kings become servants, and fires become gentle.

items.question: How does the recitation affect malefic planets and calamities?
premises: Planets become non-seizing
Calamities go to destruction
items.inference: The recitation neutralizes malefic planetary influences and destroys calamities.
uncertainties: aṇugraha may be read as anugraha in some traditions; surface retained as given
items.plain_english: Planets cease to seize, and calamities come to destruction.

items.question: Can social status or lack of knowledge prevent the reciter from avoiding sin's stain?
premises: Even one of low status may recite
Such a person is not stained by sin
items.inference: Recitation protects the practitioner from being stained by sin regardless of status or knowledge.
uncertainties: kuvarṇo interpreted as low or bad social standing; exact nuance context-dependent
items.plain_english: Even one of low status, even through knowledge, is not stained by sin.

items.question: How greatly is the merit multiplied by reciting this particular hymn?
premises: The hymn yields a specific fruit
That fruit is multiplied ten million times
items.inference: Reciting this hymn yields merit multiplied by ten million.
items.plain_english: By this hymn, that fruit is obtained multiplied ten million times.

items.question: What posthumous abode and ancestral benefit does the reciter attain?
premises: The reciter obtains residence in Vaikuṇṭha
This benefit extends to ten previous and ten later ancestors
items.inference: The reciter attains residence in Vaikuṇṭha together with twenty generations of ancestors.
items.plain_english: One obtains residence in Vaikuṇṭha along with ten previous and ten later generations.

items.question: Does praising Rāma with these divine names leave one bound to worldly existence?
premises: Some men praise with divine names
Those men are not worldly
items.inference: Those who praise with these divine names are no longer bound to worldly existence.
uncertainties: saṃsāriṇī form read as nominative plural in context
items.plain_english: Those men who praise with these divine names are not worldly beings.

items.question: To whom is the concluding obeisance of this section directed?
premises: Obeisance is offered to Raghunātha the lord
Obeisance is offered to the husband of Sītā
items.inference: The obeisance is directed to Raghunātha, the lord and husband of Sītā.
items.plain_english: Obeisance to Raghunātha, the lord, the husband of Sītā.

items.question: What ultimate spiritual attainment follows complete freedom from all sins?
premises: One becomes freed from all sins
One may obtain union with Viṣṇu
items.inference: Freedom from all sins leads to the attainment of union with Viṣṇu.
items.plain_english: Freed from all sins, one may obtain union with Viṣṇu.

items.question: Why is this teaching specifically imparted to the son of Gaṅgā?
premises: The teaching has been told to Gāṅgeya
Gāṅgeya is the best among Vaiṣṇavas
items.inference: The teaching is imparted to Gāṅgeya because he is the foremost among Vaiṣṇavas.
items.plain_english: This has been told to you, O son of Gaṅgā, because you are the best among Vaiṣṇavas.

items.question: How is Rāma characterized in relation to Jānakī and the Raghu lineage?
premises: Rāma is like sandalwood bringing joy to Jānakī's heart
Rāma is the delighter of the Raghu lineage
items.inference: Rāma brings joy to Jānakī and delight to the Raghu lineage.
items.plain_english: He is the sandalwood that brings joy to Jānakī's heart, the delighter of the Raghu line.

items.question: For what purpose did the unborn and all-pervading one manifest?
premises: The unborn all-pervading one manifested
The manifestation occurred by his own sport to protect the world
items.inference: The unborn, all-pervading Rāma manifested by his own sport to protect the world.
items.plain_english: The unborn, all-pervading one manifested by his own sport to protect the world.

items.question: What qualities of the Rāma-protection hymn motivate the wise to recite it?
premises: The wise should recite the Rāma-protection
It destroys sin and grants all desires
items.inference: The wise recite the Rāma-protection because it destroys sin and fulfills all desires.
items.plain_english: The wise should recite the Rāma-protection, which destroys sin and grants all desires.

rows.grounds: proper name nominative singular in compound context

items.question: What ritual application is prescribed for the recitation of this hymn?
premises: Śrī Rāmacandra is the deity
The application in recitation is for the pleasure of Śrī Rāmacandra
items.inference: The hymn's ritual application designates Śrī Rāmacandra as deity and aims at his pleasure.
items.plain_english: Śrī Rāmacandra is the deity; the application in recitation is for the pleasure of Śrī Rāmacandra.

items.question: Which aspects of Rāma are invoked to protect the eyes and ears?
premises: The son of Kauśalyā is asked to protect the two eyes
The one dear to Viśvāmitra is asked to protect the two ears
items.inference: Different aspects of Rāma are invoked to guard specific sense organs.
items.plain_english: May the son of Kauśalyā protect the two eyes; may the one dear to Viśvāmitra protect the two ears.

items.question: Which aspects of Rāma are invoked to protect the tongue and throat?
premises: The treasury of knowledge is asked to protect the tongue
The one honored by Bharata is asked to protect the throat
items.inference: Specific aspects of Rāma are invoked to guard the organs of speech.
uncertainties: vidyānidhiṃ taken as epithet of Rāma functioning as subject
items.plain_english: May the treasury of knowledge protect the tongue; may the one honored by Bharata protect the throat.

items.question: Which aspects of Rāma are invoked to protect the hands and heart?
premises: The lord of Sītā is asked to protect the two hands
The conqueror of Jāmadagnya is asked to protect the heart
items.inference: Specific aspects of Rāma are invoked to guard the hands and the heart.
items.plain_english: May the lord of Sītā protect the two hands; may the conqueror of Jāmadagnya protect the heart.
